summary: Extended isRawQueueEntry() in validate-entry.ts to normalize empty-string and whitespace-only expectedRepo to null (in addition to existing non-string normalization). The condition changed from `typeof e['expectedRepo'] !== 'string'` to also catch `trim().length === 0`.

Added assertSafeSegment() guard to getProjectLedgerStatus() in get-queue.ts as defense-in-depth second layer. Both slug and expectedRepo (when non-null) are now validated before any path construction — unsafe segments return { exists: false, synthesisGenerated: false } immediately. Imported assertSafeSegment from utils/path-validator.ts.
Added TC-26 and TC-27 to validate-entry.test.ts: verify empty-string and whitespace-only expectedRepo are normalized to null and entry still passes validation.

Added a new `describe('getProjectLedgerStatus — path-segment guard (this plan AC-2)', ...)` block in get-queue.test.ts with 6 test cases covering: traversal slug (..),  traversal slug with path separators, empty-string slug, traversal expectedRepo, uppercase expectedRepo, and a safe passthrough case.
All 2851 tests pass (93 test files). No regressions.

comments.note: validate-entry.ts: The `isRawQueueEntry()` function uses an inline boolean compound in the main `if` statement, which keeps validation terse but makes individual rule failures hard to pinpoint during debugging. A future refactor could extract each rule into a named predicate (e.g. `isValidId`, `isValidPid`) to improve error traceability, though this is low priority given the pure-function nature and the comprehensive test coverage.

get-queue.ts: The `assertSafeSegment()` guard in `getProjectLedgerStatus()` silently returns `{ exists: false }` on bad segments without any logging. A debug-level log message (e.g., `console.error('[getProjectLedgerStatus] Rejected unsafe segment: ...')`) would help with operational observability if a malformed entry somehow reaches this layer at runtime.

get-queue.ts: The import order now places `assertSafeSegment` after the queue-local imports. The project does not appear to enforce a strict import ordering rule, but aligning with the general pattern (node built-ins → third-party → local utils → module-local) would be consistent with how other files in src/ are structured.

Edge-case stress: SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) correctly rejects null bytes, Unicode lookalikes, path separators, and all traversal patterns. assertSafeSegment()'s Boolean(segment) guard adds explicit empty-string defense. Mixed whitespace types (tabs, newlines) are normalized by trim().length === 0 in isRawQueueEntry().

comments.note: assertSafeSegment() in path-validator.ts has a redundant Boolean(segment) guard (the regex already rejects empty strings via ^[a-z0-9] anchor). The comment in source acknowledges this as intentional defense-in-depth, which is good practice. No action needed.

getProjectLedgerStatus() silently returns { exists: false } on assertSafeSegment rejection with no log output. A debug-level log (as noted by the Developer) would improve operational observability for malformed runtime entries. Flagged as low priority — does not affect correctness.

Edge-case not currently tested: very long slugs (e.g., 500+ chars of valid [a-z0-9-] chars). assertSafeSegment passes these through to the OS path layer, which is safe since no traversal characters are permitted. No traversal risk, but an upper-bound length check could be added defensively in a future hardening pass.

summary: Reviewed 4 files (validate-entry.ts, get-queue.ts, path-validator.ts, constants.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A01 — Broken Access Control: No path traversal vulnerabilities found. assertSafeSegment() (path-validator.ts:26) uses SAFE_SLUG_REGEX (/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) which strictly whitelists only lowercase alphanumeric-and-hyphen strings anchored at both ends. Applied to both `slug` (always) and `expectedRepo` (when non-null) in getProjectLedgerStatus() before any join() call. Null bytes, Unicode lookalikes, path separators (/ and \), and traversal sequences (..) are all rejected. Defense-in-depth Boolean(segment) guard also present. No issues.

A03 — Injection: No injection surface. isRawQueueEntry() in validate-entry.ts performs strict type-checking and whitespace normalization on all fields. expectedRepo is normalized to null for empty/whitespace values (line 73). JSON.parse() output is filtered through isRawQueueEntry() before use. getProjectLedgerStatus() only reads files; it never writes, executes OS commands, or evaluates dynamic expressions. No SQL, OS command, template, or LDAP injection vectors present.

A04 — Insecure Design / Logic: Fail-safe defaults are correct throughout. readQueueFile() returns [] on any I/O or parse error. getProjectLedgerStatus() returns { exists: false, synthesisGenerated: false } on I/O error, parse error, and invalid segment — the safe direction in all cases. isRawQueueEntry() rejects missing or non-positive PID, ensuring no zombie PID zero (kill(0, 0) would signal the calling process group). No logic flaws identified.

A02/A05/A06/A07/A08/A09/A10 — Not applicable to this changeset. The two modified source files (validate-entry.ts, get-queue.ts) contain no cryptographic operations, authentication logic, session handling, deserialization of untrusted objects beyond JSON.parse() (safely filtered post-parse), or outbound HTTP/network calls. No new dependencies were introduced. No secrets, credentials, or PII fields are present. SSRF is not applicable — all file paths are constructed from server-controlled ledgerRoot + validated segments.

Info — Unbounded slug length: assertSafeSegment() (path-validator.ts:26) enforces character set but no maximum length. Very long valid slugs (e.g., 500+ chars of [a-z0-9-]) pass through to the OS path layer. Since no traversal characters are permitted this is not exploitable for path traversal, but an upper-bound limit (e.g., 128 chars) would be a low-effort hardening improvement for a future pass. No immediate risk.

Info — Silent rejection in getProjectLedgerStatus() (get-queue.ts:131-135): assertSafeSegment() failures return { exists: false } with no log output. A debug-level log entry would improve operational observability for diagnosing malformed queue entries in production. No security impact — the safe-fail behavior is correct.

summary: Reviewed all 4 modified files: validate-entry.ts, get-queue.ts, validate-entry.test.ts, get-queue.test.ts. Plus path-validator.ts (read-only context).

Maintainability: Both source changes are minimal and well-scoped. isRawQueueEntry() mutation side-effect is extensively documented in JSDoc — no surprise to future readers. assertSafeSegment guards in getProjectLedgerStatus() have clear inline comments. No over-engineering.

Best Practices: Whitelist regex approach (SAFE_SLUG_REGEX /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/) is the correct pattern. Defense-in-depth layering (normalization at isRawQueueEntry() + guard at getProjectLedgerStatus()) is architecturally sound and resilient to call-site bypass. Fail-safe defaults are consistent and correct throughout.
Performance: No concerns. Both additions are trivially cheap (regex test, string trim, no new I/O).

Future Context: Aligned with multi-root workspace direction. The explicit second-layer guard future-proofs against callers that may invoke getProjectLedgerStatus() directly without routing through isRawQueueEntry(). Test coverage is thorough — 6 guard cases + 2 normalization cases.
